rating_cap: No headline-rating lock; conviction is capped at 65 because a bank-specific solvency conclusion is unavailable. No Critical red flag exists.
variant_perception_summary: Nu's fast growth and strong Q2 are known, and the sell side remains constructive. The provisional difference is that current spread and revenue gains arrive before the full credit-loss outcome, H1 net income included a large deferred-tax benefit, and the current price exceeds every engine fair-value case. The edge is not proven because the Group required return is unresolved.
what_everyone_knows: Nu is a fast-growing Latin American digital bank with 139 million Q2 customers, 83.5% activity, and strong Q2 revenue and EPS growth.
what_is_priced_in: US$14.30 and a US$18.78 mean sell-side target reflect continued high growth and returns. A clean reverse read is unavailable; conditional on a 16.51% Brazil Investments CGU rate, the price requires 47.36% terminal ROE or 80.89% FY2027–30 profit growth, while 9.78% reconciles the same path.
what_market_may_be_missing: Current credit-income and lower-credit-cost benefits may precede later losses, and the US$991.046m H1 deferred-tax benefit makes the period less cash-backed than headline net income suggests; neither point proves improper accounting.
edge_proof: The skeptical edge is supported if a model-consistent Group cost of equity remains above the rate needed to justify US$14.30 and Q3 misses a raised bar or shows worse credit quality. It is falsified by a clean Group valuation at or above US$14.30 and a material Q3 dual beat with stable or better delinquency, credit cost, and expected-credit-loss coverage.
killer_risk: The residual-income duration or required return is wrong; sustained residual earnings or a lower Group cost of equity could make US$8.47 too low.

red_flags.description: Five High findings converge on one credit-cycle risk: spread durability, the raised FQ3 bar, lender-specific cash/accrual divergence, the US$991.046m deferred-tax benefit, and the US$504.700m downside-macro allowance bound. These are not proof of a misstatement.
KPMG Brazil was censured and fined US$700,000 by the PCAOB for work involving another issuer; Nu was not named. Nu's FY2023–FY2025 audit opinions were clean and FY2025 ICFR was effective.

Recurring share-based compensation is excluded from adjusted net income; the FY2025 US$359.0m addback produced a US$203.7m after-tax or 7.1% uplift. This is a candor concern, not evidence of misstatement.
